verses.note: Abram's scruple does not become a burden he lays on others. As the leader of the expedition he treats his treaty partners fairly, giving them their due share, a principle David later makes law for those who stay behind with the baggage (1 Samuel 30:24-25).

Judah begins to lead by telling his father an unwelcome truth. He does not flatter Jacob's grief or hide the terms; he names the cost of refusal. This is the first step in the change that will make Judah the family's spokesman in chapter 44.
Judah leads by stepping into the place of danger himself, not by commanding others. The brother who once proposed the sale of Joseph now stands between the ruler and the youngest brother.
